title: PPDA Releases Revised Procurement Thresholds — What Construction Firms Must Know
excerpt: The Public Procurement and Disposal of Public Assets Authority has published revisions to financial thresholds governing works contracts. Contractors and consultants should review immediately.
body:
The Public Procurement and Disposal of Public Assets Authority has published revisions to the financial thresholds that govern how works contracts are advertised and awarded. Contractors and consultants bidding for public work should read them before their next submission.

## What has changed

[image:1|Rebar moved most in September.]

Thresholds determine which procurement method an entity must use for a contract of a given value. Raise them and more work can be awarded through simplified methods; lower them and more goes to open bidding.

The practical effect for a mid-sized contractor is in which notices you now qualify to see, and how much documentation a submission requires.

## What to do about it

- Check which threshold band your usual contract size now falls into
- Confirm your registration and tax clearance are current before the next advertisement, not after
- If you bid through a joint venture, review whether the arrangement still meets the requirement at the new band

> Read the notice on the PPDA portal rather than relying on a summary. Thresholds are exact figures and a paraphrase is not a defence if you submit under the wrong method.

## Our view

Threshold changes tend to be reported as either good or bad news for contractors. In practice they mostly redistribute: the firms that benefit are those whose paperwork is already in order on the day the change takes effect.

title: Kampala Flyover Phase 2: Tender Released, Construction to Begin Q4
excerpt: The second phase of the Kampala flyover project has been formally tendered. Expressions of interest close at the end of the month.
body:
The second phase of the Kampala flyover project has been formally tendered, with expressions of interest closing at the end of the month.

## Scope

Phase two extends the works begun under the first phase, covering additional junctions and associated drainage, utility relocation and pedestrian provision.

## Why it matters beyond the main contractor

A project of this size moves the market around it. Steel, aggregate and formwork demand rise locally, plant hire tightens, and experienced site staff become harder to keep. Firms with no involvement in the contract will still feel it in their input costs.

- Expect pressure on structural steel and rebar pricing
- Plant hire rates typically firm up within the quarter
- Skilled site supervisors become scarce and more expensive

## What to do now

If you price work in Kampala over the next eighteen months, build a materials escalation assumption into quotations rather than absorbing it. The firms that get hurt by a project like this are the ones that quoted a fixed price in the month before it started.

title: Steel Prices Rise 8% — Industry Response to Shilling Weakness
excerpt: Structural steel prices in Kampala have climbed by approximately 8% over the past 60 days, driven by currency pressure and regional demand.
body:
Structural steel prices in Kampala have climbed by approximately eight per cent over the past sixty days, driven by currency pressure and regional demand.

## What the movement looks like

Our weekly price index has recorded steady increases across rebar and sections, with the sharpest movement in 16mm rebar. The rise has been gradual rather than a single jump, which is why several firms have told us they only noticed when re-ordering.

## Why it is happening

Two things are pushing at once. Shilling weakness raises the landed cost of imported billet and finished sections. Regional infrastructure demand is competing for the same supply.

## What it means for a live job

- A quotation more than sixty days old is now materially under-priced on steel
- Fixed-price contracts without an escalation clause absorb this entirely
- Ordering early is only worth it if you have somewhere dry to store it

> If you are pricing now, quote steel separately with a validity period rather than folding it into a lump sum. Clients dislike it less than a variation later.

## Watch the index

We update material prices every Wednesday from the same three Kampala suppliers, so the series is comparable week to week. The underlying dataset is available if you need it for a claim or a forecast.

title: ARB and ERB Announce Mandatory CPD Requirements
excerpt: Architects and engineers on the ARB and ERB registers will be required to complete 40 CPD hours annually beginning next year.
body:
Architects and engineers on the ARB and ERB registers will be required to complete forty hours of continuing professional development each year, beginning next year.

## The requirement

Forty CPD hours annually, recorded and submitted at renewal. What counts toward the total includes structured training, recognised conferences, and certain forms of documented professional activity.

## Practical points

- Start recording now rather than reconstructing a year later
- Keep evidence: attendance records, certificates, programmes
- Check which providers your board recognises before paying for a course

## For firms rather than individuals

If you employ registered professionals, their CPD is now a scheduling and budgeting matter for you as well. Forty hours is roughly a week of working time per person per year.

> Firms that treat CPD as an administrative chore tend to leave it to December. Those that treat it as training get something back for money they had to spend anyway.

## Verifying a registration

Both registers are public. If you are engaging a professional and their registration matters to the work, check it directly rather than relying on a letterhead.
